newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Churchill port shipping season ends - CWB.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Churchill port shipping season ends - CWB.

text.p: Canada's Hudson Bay Port of Churchill ended its 1996 shipping season on Monday, a Canadian Wheat Board official said.
"One ship cleared Churchill Monday carrying 14,000 tonnes of grain. That ends our (export) program out of there," CWB spokesman Brian Stacey said in a telephone interview.
The port loaded 305,000 tonnes of wheat and barley on a dozen ships bound for Mexico, Brazil and Egypt in the 88 days it operated this year, Stacey said.
Churchill needs to ship 600,000 tonnes to break even, a federal report on the port issued in 1993 stated.
Canadian National Railway Co plans to sell the rail line that carries grain cars to Churchill, CN president Paul Tellier told Reuters on Oct 1.
